html:
The Constitution of Kenya of 2010 is the supreme law of Kenya. Voters approved it in a referendum on 4 August 2010, and it was proclaimed on 27 August.

It replaced the independence constitution of 1963, which successive presidents, from Jomo Kenyatta on, had amended to gather power in their own hands. Demands for a new one ran through the 1990s and 2000s. A first draft was rejected in a 2005 referendum. Then the bloodshed after the 2007 election, the 2007 to 2008 crisis, made reform urgent, and the power-sharing deal under President Mwai Kibaki led to the new text.

Its main changes:

  • power devolved to 47 elected county governments;
  • a Senate to speak for the counties;
  • a long bill of rights, including social and economic rights;
  • an independent judiciary with a new Supreme Court, and limits on presidential power.

The new courts showed their teeth in 2017, when the Supreme Court annulled a presidential election, a first in Africa.
sum: The Constitution of Kenya of 2010 is the supreme law of Kenya. Voters approved it in a referendum on 4 August 2010, and it was proclaimed on 27 August.
